# From Textual Columns to Query Plans: A Unified Relational-Semantic Execution Framework for Hybrid Query Processing

## Research question

Queries over hybrid tables may require attributes hidden in text, while vague language admits several schema mappings or computational interpretations.

## Method

The system prunes and profiles schemas, constructs query-aware data previews, and generates alternative operator DAGs. Relational steps execute through SQL; semantic extraction, filtering, joining and aggregation use LLMs. Optimization and batching reduce costs, then a judge or semantic vote selects one candidate answer.

## Evaluation

RepairTQA supplies paired structured and textual representations; five additional table-QA benchmarks test transfer. Evaluation uses 100 examples per dataset/subset, except 50 for multi-table long. Reference-based LLM scoring measures answer correctness; reference-free candidate selection and oracle ACC@6 are reported separately.

## What the results support

Diversification outperforms naive plan sampling in the displayed ablations, and optimization lowers token cost without changing those accuracy scores. The main RepairTQA comparison reports higher selected-answer accuracy, but gains do not hold against every baseline on every extended benchmark.

## Limits and qualifications

No user clarification, refusal policy or all-interpretation coverage is evaluated. Model-based answer scoring can err, and preprocessing may discard information. Confidence intervals use aggregate accuracies and nominal sample sizes rather than repeated-run variation. K/batch-size accuracy curves use oracle ACC@K. Token measurements do not establish end-to-end latency or semantic preservation guarantees.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An adjacent implementation direction for recovering missing structure and exploring alternative groundings before committing to an answer, with user-intent validation still unresolved.
